chunks: Ibn Abi Umeyr, from Basheer, from Ibn Abi Yafour, who said:

I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) when a man from our companions entered upon him and said to him, 'May Allah keep you well. Indeed, sometimes the man from among us is afflicted by financial straitness or difficulty, and he is summoned to construction; he builds it, or to a canal; he rents/digs it, or to a dam; he repairs it. So what do you say regarding that?'

So Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) said: 'I do not like that I should tie a knot for them, or tie up a bag for them, and that for me is what is between its two ends. No, and not (even) for a circumflex with a pen. Indeed, the assistants of the unjust, on the Day of Resurrection, will be in pavilions of Fire until Allah judges between the servants.'

key_terms.النَّهَرِ: Canal or river (often referring to irrigation works)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on working for the unjust ruler in construction when facing financial hardship?
ai.summary: Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that while working for the unjust ruler in construction is permissible during financial hardship, it carries the spiritual weight of being an 'assistant of the unjust' (aw'an al-zalima). This status places them in 'pavilions of fire' (suradq) awaiting divine judgment, a concept rooted in the hadith's specific phrasing 'la wa la dawman bi-qalam' (no, nor even a moment's delay with a pen), emphasizing the certainty of their recompense. This ruling highlights the Shia distinction between mere permissibility and the higher virtue of avoiding political complicity, even for livelihood.

en.hubeali: Ibn Abu Umeyr, from Basheer, from Ibn Abu Yafour who said,

‘I was in the presence of Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> when a man came over from our companions, so he said to him<sup>asws</sup>, ‘May Allah<sup>azwj</sup> Keep you<sup>asws</sup> well! Sometimes the man from among us is hit by the (financial) straitness, or the difficulty, and he is summoned (by the unjust governor) to the construction which he builds, or the canal which he digs, or the dam which he corrects. So what are you<sup>asws</sup> saying regarding that?’

So Abu Abdullahasws said: ‘Iasws do not like it that Iasws should tie a knot for them, or tie up a bag for them, and that for measws is what is between its final (end result). No, and not (even) for a circumflex (a mark on a letter like Fatah, Kisra etc.) with a pen. The supporters of the unjust, on the Day of Judgement, would be in pavilions of Fire until Allahazwj has Judged between the (other) servants’.
en.sarwar: 7. Ibn abu ‘Umayr has narrated from Bashir from ibn abu Ya’fur who has said the following:

“Once I was in the presence of abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, when a certain man of our people came and said, ‘I pray to Allah to keep you well, one of us may face hardship and straitened conditions and is called to construct a building, work a canal or a dam. What is your decision in such case?

He (the Imam) replied, ‘I do not like it. I have knotted for them a knot and tied down the opening end of the bag of ‘no’. It is no and not even the moving of a pen. The helpers of the unjust ones on the Day of Judgment will be kept in chambers of fire until Allah will judge all of His servants.’”
